sources.entry: AudioMIDI - Converts short melodies or solo-instrument audio into editable MIDI with browser note preview and export; no-signup Quick mode and three free Deep transcriptions per day. #free #music #midi

summary.name: AudioMIDI
summary.one_liner: A browser-based tool that converts short MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG or M4A melody recordings into editable MIDI files with a note preview.
use_cases: Convert a short piano or guitar melody into editable MIDI
Transcribe a sung or solo-instrument melody to notes
Get a MIDI file to import into a DAW for correction
Check detected notes against a recording before arranging
Extract a melody from a clear excerpt of a song
summary.what_it_does: Accepts an audio recording of up to 5 minutes and 25 MB, decodes it in the browser, and estimates the notes as a preview that can be compared with the source. The Studio lets you audition the detected phrase with a selectable playback sound and download a .mid file. The default browser path keeps audio on the device without an account, while a separate high-accuracy server route requires explicit consent to upload. The page says results are best for short clear single-instrument or solo-vocal melodies and that dense mixes need manual correction in a DAW.
notable: Runs in the browser; default conversion keeps audio on the device with no sign-up
Quick mode has no daily allowance; high-accuracy server mode gives 3 free transcriptions per day (UTC reset)
Note preview and playback sound selection in the Studio before downloading MIDI
Accepts MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG and M4A inputs, with WAV/Song/Audio variants
caveats: Limited to recordings up to 5 minutes and 25 MB; dense mixes and songs need manual correction
High-accuracy mode is limited to 3 free transcriptions per day, shared across the same public network
Output is note data only; it does not recover the original voice, microphone sound or full mix, and MP3 compression cannot be undone by converting to WAV
